newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu, PLO's Arafat end Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu, PLO's Arafat end Hebron talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat ended three and a half hours of U.S.-mediated talks on Tuesday on an Israeli troop pullout from the West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.
They said Arafat left without making any comment to reporters.
U.S. sources said Arafat left for Christmas Eve celebrations in the West Bank town of Bethlehem.

The witnesses said Arafat smiled and waved as he left the meeting at the Israel-Gaza border, but declined to answer reporters' questions on whether an agreement had been reached on the long-delayed Israeli troop pullout from Hebron.
The sources said U.S. President Bill Clinton's peace envoy Dennis Ross would make an announcement regarding the talks "in a short time."

Ross said earlier that the talks had been "clearly energised" during his mediation mission which began on Saturday, but that he did not expect one meeting would be enough to conclude the elusive agreement.
